title: Shared recipe collections
deliverable: Add server-backed folders/tags and permission-aware recipe sharing without default input sharing.
acceptance: Revoking access prevents future reads; links and searches cannot enumerate another workspace.

title: Shared-collection search integration
deliverable: Extend the already-qualified repository and Meilisearch search projections to server collections, sharing and revision policies through the same SearchService contract.
acceptance: Both backends pass collection-sharing, inherited/revoked grants, revision edits, stale-index and recovery tests; names/tags remain an approved projection and secret-bearing collection metadata is excluded.

title: Recipe revisions and conflicts
deliverable: Add optimistic revision checks, compare/restore and explicit multi-client conflict handling.
acceptance: Two clients cannot silently overwrite each other; no real-time collaboration framework is required.

title: Administrative policy
deliverable: Add operation/pack allowlists, egress policy, resource profiles and retention settings.
acceptance: Policy is enforced server-side and reported through capabilities; clients cannot self-authorize forbidden operations.

title: Audit and retention lifecycle
deliverable: Add bounded audit export, retention jobs, object deletion and backup-retention documentation.
acceptance: Payloads are absent by default; deleted live records and retained backups are not misleadingly described as immediate erasure everywhere.

title: Logical storage export
deliverable: Export portable recipe, identity-reference, job and artifact manifests using versioned logical records.
acceptance: Export is independent of PostgreSQL SQL syntax and contains explicit integrity/referential checks.

title: MySQL portability prototype
deliverable: Implement actual MySQL repository methods and backend-specific migrations in a separate adapter.
acceptance: Shared contracts run against a real MySQL instance; merely compiling a generic driver is insufficient.

title: SQL semantic parity
deliverable: Exercise collation, uniqueness, JSON values, booleans, timestamps, pagination and transaction behavior on both databases.
acceptance: Results and conflict semantics agree despite different SQL dialects; deviations stay inside adapters.

title: PostgreSQL-to-MySQL migration drill
deliverable: Import a logical export into MySQL, verify hashes/counts/references, rehearse cutover and rollback.
acceptance: Application use cases work without domain or API changes; failures leave the original deployment recoverable.

title: MySQL-to-PostgreSQL reverse drill
deliverable: Reimport the same logical model and repeat repository and authorization tests.
acceptance: Round trips retain identifiers/revisions; the project makes no unsupported zero-downtime migration guarantee.

title: Artifact backend portability
deliverable: Exercise local-disk and an optional object-storage adapter against the same artifact contracts.
acceptance: Range reads, integrity, leases and orphan cleanup work without tying metadata schema to one cloud provider.

title: Backup and disaster recovery
deliverable: Document and test coordinated metadata/artifact backups, schema recovery and corruption detection.
acceptance: Restore drills actually read and execute restored recipes/artifacts instead of only checking backup file existence.

title: Release packaging
deliverable: Produce versioned static offline bundles, native API binaries and container images with manifests and notices.
acceptance: Builds identify exact dependency and operation-pack revisions; no desktop/mobile application is shipped yet.

title: Upgrade and rollback
deliverable: Add compatible server/browser/pack upgrade rules, migration prechecks and rollback guidance.
acceptance: An interrupted upgrade cannot mix incompatible schema/engine assets or corrupt saved recipes.

title: Operational load qualification
deliverable: Exercise realistic multi-user mixes, expensive-job fairness, disk pressure and process failure.
acceptance: Published limits come from measurements; API responsiveness survives isolated worker exhaustion.

title: Portability and operations gate
deliverable: Close deployment docs, actual second-database contract tests and Vef/Brynja replacement rehearsals.
acceptance: PostgreSQL is the initial production-supported backend; MySQL support level is stated separately from the proven portability contract.

title: Integrated service recovery gate
deliverable: Rehearse coordinated PostgreSQL/artifact restore, OpenBao recovery/rotation, Valkey cold start and optional search rebuild.
acceptance: A restored deployment serves authorized recipes and can run them; cache/search loss does not lose authoritative data; all recovery steps are automated or explicitly custody-gated.
